The One Big Beautiful Bill's pro-family provisions are a rare example of Washington prioritizing taxpayers over bureaucracy. The Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit expansion puts $2,940 back in working families' pockets—real relief after decades of inflationary neglect. Doubling DCAP flexible spending accounts to $7,500 forces employers to compete for talent through childcare support rather than relying on bloated federal programs.

But let’s be clear: these wins only happened because the bill redirected $56B previously wasted on Medicaid fraud and illegal alien healthcare costs. Permanent 50% tax credits for employer childcare facilities will finally incentivize private sector solutions over bureaucratic handouts.

The lesson? When you stop funding failure (Biden’s Medicaid expansion) and start rewarding productivity (Trump’s CDCTC reforms), Americans thrive. Now audit every line item to ensure these provisions aren’t diluted by career bureaucrats.
